items.followUp: Name the five basic elements of a data communication system.

rubric.why: Identifies the communicating parties.
rubric.description: Names the sender and receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both sender and receiver.

rubric.why: Identifies what is communicated and how communication is governed.
rubric.description: Names the message, transmission medium, and protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all three remaining components.

modelAnswer: The components of a communication system are sender, receiver, message, transmission medium, and protocol.

items.followUp: What is HTTP, and what is it used for?

rubric.why: Gives the full form of FTP.
rubric.description: Expands FTP as File Transfer Protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form.

rubric.why: Explains the protocol’s purpose.
rubric.description: States that FTP is used to transfer files between computers over a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing file transfer between computers or over a network.

modelAnswer: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol.
It is a protocol used to transfer files between computers over a network.

rubric.why: Explains how a hyperlink is used.
rubric.description: States that a hyperlink is a clickable element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as clickable text or an image.

rubric.why: Explains what the hyperlink points to.
rubric.description: States that it connects to another web page, document, or location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a destination or linked resource.

modelAnswer: A hyperlink is clickable text or an image in a document or web page.
When clicked, it takes the user to another web page, document, or location.

items.followUp: Define an algorithm and explain the use of the decision and input/output symbols in a flowchart.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of a flowchart.
rubric.description: Defines a flowchart as a graphical representation of an algorithm or solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition that identifies a graphical representation of steps or an algorithm.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the terminal symbol.
rubric.description: Explains that the oval symbol shows the start or end.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and use.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the process symbol.
rubric.description: Explains that the rectangle represents a process, calculation, or instruction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and use.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the input/output symbol.
rubric.description: Explains that the parallelogram represents input or output.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct symbol and use.

modelAnswer: A flowchart is a graphical representation of the steps of an algorithm or solution to a problem, using standard symbols and arrows.
The oval (terminal) symbol represents the start or end of a flowchart.
The rectangle (process) symbol represents an instruction, operation, or calculation.
The parallelogram represents input or output.

items.followUp: Describe two advantages of connecting computers in a network.

rubric.why: Checks whether the student identifies sharing of physical resources.
rubric.description: Explains that a network allows hardware or devices to be shared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant hardware-sharing example.

rubric.why: Checks whether the student identifies sharing of digital resources.
rubric.description: Explains that users can share files, data, or software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant digital-resource-sharing point.

rubric.why: Checks whether the student identifies communication as a purpose of networking.
rubric.description: Explains that a network enables communication between users or computers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant communication point.

rubric.why: Checks whether the student identifies another practical benefit of networking.
rubric.description: Explains that a network can provide access to information or shared Internet resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant access or information-sharing benefit.

modelAnswer: A computer network connects computers so that users can share hardware, such as printers and storage devices.
Users can share files, data, and software through the network.
A network enables communication and exchange of messages between users.
It can provide users with access to shared information and Internet resources.

items.followUp: What is software piracy? Give two examples of its types.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of software piracy.
rubric.description: Defines software piracy as unauthorized copying or use of copyrighted software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition that identifies unauthorized copying or use.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of a recognized type of piracy.
rubric.description: Identifies softlifting: installing or sharing a licensed program beyond the licence terms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and explaining one valid type.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of another type of piracy.
rubric.description: Identifies another recognized type, such as hard-disk loading, counterfeiting, or Internet piracy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and explaining a second valid type.

rubric.why: Checks that the note explains the harmful or unlawful nature of piracy.
rubric.description: States that piracy violates the software owner’s rights or licence conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the practice is unauthorized or violates licence or copyright rules.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the unauthorized copying, distribution, or use of copyrighted software.
Softlifting is installing or sharing a licensed program in a way that exceeds the licence terms.
Hard-disk loading is installing unauthorized copies of software on computers sold to customers.
Counterfeiting is making and selling copies of software that are presented as genuine.
These practices violate the software owner’s copyright or licence conditions.

items.followUp: State two ways a flowchart helps when solving a problem.

rubric.why: Checks the flowchart’s role in making a solution easier to understand.
rubric.description: Explains that a flowchart presents the solution steps or logic visually.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant explanation of visual clarity or understanding.

rubric.why: Checks another practical benefit during problem solving.
rubric.description: Explains that flowcharts help find errors, communicate a solution, or document it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one relevant benefit beyond visual presentation.

modelAnswer: A flowchart presents the steps and logic of a solution visually, making the problem easier to understand.
It helps locate errors and makes the solution easier to communicate or document.

items.followUp: What two resources are considered when assessing the efficiency of an algorithm?

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the time resource used to assess efficiency.
rubric.description: Identifies the time taken by the algorithm as a measure of efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning execution time or time taken.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the memory resource used to assess efficiency.
rubric.description: Identifies the memory or space used by the algorithm as a measure of efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning memory or space usage.

modelAnswer: The efficiency of an algorithm is judged by the resources it uses to solve a problem.
The main resources considered are the time taken to execute and the memory or space used.
